newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 17.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

News Corp's "Return of the Jedi," the third installment in the "Star Wars" trilogy, completed a clean sweep for the series' reissue by taking top spot at the box office over the weekend, according to estimates Sunday.

WMC Ltd, Japan's Mitsui Group and Brazilian iron ore miner MBR are looking to team up to bid in the privatization auction of Brazil's CVRD, a Brazilian news agency said. WMC Chief Executive Hugh Morgan, who is currently in Brazil, said his company was looking into forming a consortium with Mitsui and Mineracoes Brasileiras Reunidas (MBR) to bid for a strategic stake in Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), Agencia Estado said. * Coles Myer Ltd A$5.86 (-0.07)

Coles Myer Ltd Chief Executive Dennis Eck said on Sunday a break up of the giant retailer was likely to always shadow the company but it was not actively considering it at the moment. Eck also said Coles Myer had no immediate plans for a share buy-back, saying more capital needed to be spent refurbishing its Kmart discount variety stores and Myer Grace Bros department stores.

National Australia Bank Ltd said late on Friday it would raise US$875 million from a global offering of exchangeable capital units, up from the planned US$750 million raising announced in November 1996.
Casinos Austria International Ltd (CAIL) said late on Friday it expects market condistions in 1997 to continue to be difficult after reporting a net loss of A$18.47 million in calendar 1996.
